question: A body is thrown up and it reaches a height of 5m and then falls down, the total displacement and the total distance covered by the body respectively would be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0m, 10m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Displacement** is the shortest distance between the initial and final position of the body.
 
• **Total displacement** is 0m because the body returns to its starting point.
 
• **Distance** is the total path covered by the body.
 
• **Total distance** covered is 10m, as it travels 5m up and 5m down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement vs Distance**

 
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity with both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Distance** is a scalar quantity and only considers the magnitude.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall**
 
 
• It is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In free fall, the body gains speed as it descends.
 
 
 
• **Projectile Motion**
 
 
• It involves objects thrown into the air, affected by gravity and air resistance.
 
• The motion can be analyzed in two dimensions: horizontal and vertical.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration Due to Gravity**
 
 
• The acceleration experienced by an object due to Earth's gravitational pull is approximately 9.8 m/s².
 
• This value remains constant near the surface of the Earth.
